Now, the one remaining risk: correctness of the equivalence "answers equal LPM over all image rules". Let me prove more carefully to ensure no weird case where traversal would miss a matching rule that LPM finds.

Given valid image. Consider rule r: prefix P with length L, hop H, located in stage i with node N at depth b=c[i], and b < L <= e=c[i+1]. Node N has prefix trunc(P,b) (must, by layout: rules under node with trunc(rule,b)==node key). For an address A matching P (A's first L bits == P), does traversal reach node N?
- At stage 0, node root; check rules there. Any rule in root with length<=c1 matching A collected.
- Follow edge in root whose prefix trunc(q,c1) matches A for some FIB descendant q length>c1. P itself has length L. If L>c1, then P is a descendant; trunc(P,c1) edge exists in root (since P.length>c1 and trunc(P,0)=root). A matches trunc(P,c1) because A matches P's first L≥c1 bits. So traversal follows edge trunc(P,c1) → node at stage1 = trunc(P,c1). Continue similarly. Since L>b for all stages before i (because c[i]=b < L), at each stage j<i the edge trunc(P,c[j+1]) exists and A matches. So reach node at stage i = trunc(P,b)=N. Collect r. Good.
- If some stage e >= L before reaching i? Stage i is where b<L<=e, so for j<i, c[j+1] <= c[i]=b < L, so L>c[j+1], edge exists. Good.

Thus any rule matching A is collected during traversal. Conversely, traversal only collects rules actually matching A (we check match). And rules at node N collected are only those whose prefix matches A. So traversal's best = LPM. Also traversal may stop early if no edge matches; but then there are no deeper FIB prefixes matching A, so no deeper rules match A; rules beyond not collected but they wouldn't match anyway. Actually if no edge matches at stage i, could there be a rule at deeper stage j>i matching A? Such rule has prefix Q with trunc(Q,c[i+1]) = some edge in node N (since Q.length>c[i+1] and under N). If A matches Q then A matches trunc(Q,c[i+1]) → edge matches, contradiction. So none. Good.

So LPM over all rules = traversal result. Direct LPM correct.

Now, another subtle: The rules collected across stages define FIB; a rule's node key trunc(P,b) and placement check. Good.
